mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS increasing over the past month) compresses equity valuations by raising discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS increases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that may trigger aggressive monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE falls below 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, but only when the federal funds rate is not rising.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase, and FEDFUNDS not rising
regime_hint: strong consumer demand with stable monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS both increase and FEDFUNDS is not rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a supply shock that reduces corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increasing level of housing starts (HOUST rising over the past month) signals robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when HOUST rises, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 5.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises above 5.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), the Federal Reserve's policy actions compress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods during monetary tightening cycles, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
